area: integrations/google-drive-brain.md + the knowledge-fabric deck tile + brain-learn-daily / openjarvis task descriptions

The knowledge-fabric tile counts a 'Drive folder' store that reads 0 files on every sample; brain-learn-daily's description says it 'distills his personal Google Drive Second Brain folder'; openjarvis's says it 'indexes the Obsidian vault + redacted Drive brain folder'. No Drive credential, connector or client exists for any of them to use, and the redaction step those descriptions promise has never been built. Every other component Steven named in that request (Orca/Jarvis/Ruflo, Notion, Graphify, Obsidian, RAG, ECC) is real. Confirmed independently 2026-09-22: grep for 'google.?drive' across the repo returns 7 files, none of which is a connector, client or credential path; MAC-SETUP.sh has no gdrive step and creates no ~/.config/gdrive/.env; mac-verify.sh has no Drive check. recall-cache.md already lists 'a store the fabric count says is at 0 — e.g. the Drive folder' as an ALERT condition, so the alarm has been firing into a void.

(a) Wire it via path A in google-drive-brain.md: Google Drive for Desktop already mounts the folder at ~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-<account>/…, so point the existing indexer at that path — no API, no OAuth, no new egress surface. Do not leave it as-is: a 0-file store rendered as a live store is a false green on the deck.

area: MAC-INSTALL-comms-data.md §1 — PyPI name collision for whatsapp-cli
finding: `pip install whatsapp-cli` installs yausername/whatsapp-cli 0.1.3 ('CLI for whatsapp', MIT), an unrelated project — not marcelrgberger/whatsapp-cli 1.0.0, which is the one the WhatsApp channel depends on and which is not published to PyPI at all. This is the same class of trap as the Agent Reach one already documented in MAC-INSTALL-tooling.md §11, and it had never been written down. The installer itself is SAFE — MAC-SETUP.sh:435 installs from the clone's agent-harness directory, never by PyPI name — so nothing is currently broken; the risk is a future 'simplification' of a clone-plus-build into a one-line pip install.
evidence: pypi.org/pypi/whatsapp-cli/json on 2026-09-22: version 0.1.3, author 'yausername', home_page https://github.com/yausername/whatsapp-cli. marcelrgberger/whatsapp-cli resolves live via git ls-remote but publishes no PyPI distribution under that name. MAC-SETUP.sh:429 clones the repo and :435 runs `uv pip install --python "$WA_DIR/.venv/bin/python" "$WA_DIR/agent-harness"` — a path, not a name.
fix: CLOSED by P6: a **Trap** paragraph added to MAC-INSTALL-comms-data.md §1 immediately above the install block, matching the wording pattern §11 already uses for Agent Reach, and stating explicitly that the install must never be reduced to `pip install whatsapp-cli`.

area: Coverage of the whole list against the Mac — nothing here has ever executed on the target
finding: Nine items are classified Installable, meaning a real installer line points at a live upstream. Not one of them has run on Steven's Mac. Every sandbox verification behind them — including the one this session added for Laya — was performed on Linux in a throwaway prefix, against a different CPU architecture, a different Python build channel and, for anything touching macOS APIs (whatsapp-cli's ChatStorage.sqlite read, the System Events send path, launchd, Full Disk Access), a platform where the code path cannot even be reached. The first real run of MAC-SETUP.sh is still the first real test of the entire list, and mac-verify.sh has correspondingly never produced a meaningful result.
evidence: MAC-SETUP.sh header comment line 23: 'Not executed on a Mac by its author'. mac-verify.sh prints 'not macOS — the launchd, permission and WhatsApp checks cannot mean anything here' when uname is not Darwin. docs/findings/findings-M3.json enumerates line by line what is untested. P6's own Laya proof ran on Linux x86_64 CPython 3.11.15 and pulled CUDA wheels a Mac would never see (a Mac gets the CPU/MPS torch build).
fix: On the Mac, in this order: `./MAC-SETUP.sh --dry-run` and read it in full; then `./MAC-SETUP.sh --only codeburn` to baseline the spend; then the rest without --only; then `./mac-verify.sh` and treat its first output as the real inventory. Expect failures — that is the point of the first run. Do not update any deck row to 'live' until mac-verify.sh has actually exited 0 for that tool.
